clue.text: Cancels phones backstage

parts.note: to phone someone is to call them, so phones gives calls
in theatre, off (offstage) means out of sight of the audience, behind the scenes

explanation.surface: Someone backstage at a theatre rings round to call off a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To call something off is an idiom for abandoning it, the same as cancelling it.

clue.text: Frank and I cutting disc

indicators.note: the words placed into the middle cut the disc's letters in two

parts.note: CD, compact disc

explanation.surface: Someone named Frank is cutting a record with the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name but is the adjective. 'cutting' puts AND and I between the C and D of CD.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid and frank are synonyms, both meaning open and honest in speech.

clue.text: English car transports goods and snacks

parts.note: G stands for good, so doubled GG stands for goods
a Rolls, short for Rolls-Royce, is a car

explanation.surface: An English motor is used to deliver goods and some snack food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transports' is only a link joining the pieces: E, then GG, then ROLLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg rolls are a Chinese-restaurant food item, eaten as light bites or starters.

clue.text: Stop going east and west

definitions.note: to halt a car at the roadside, the same sense the palindromic letters carry when read in either direction

indicators.note: the letters read the same whichever way along the across row you travel, from left or from right

parts.note: to halt a car at the roadside, the same sense the palindromic letters carry when read in either direction

explanation.surface: An order to halt, whichever direction one is travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across entry, west to east is left to right, so a word that reads the same both ways goes east and west.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull up is an idiom for a vehicle halting, i.e. coming to a stop.

clue.text: Cooks absurdly overdue masterpieces

parts.note: chefs are cooks

indicators.note: arranged absurdly, the letters of overdue are put into a nonsensical new order

explanation.surface: Chefs whose masterpieces arrive ridiculously late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absurdly' rearranges OVERDUE into DOEUVRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef-d'oeuvre is French for a crowning work; the plural matches the plural masterpieces.

clue.text: Motif left over at end of page

indicators.note: turned over, the word is read from its last letter back to its first

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A design motif runs over at the foot of a page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns PORT into TROP, then E closes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trope is a recurring theme or device, much like a motif in art or literature.

clue.text: Ties up parcels at home? Such jobs are easy

indicators.note: here a verb: the outer word wraps up the inner one like a parcel

parts.note: to tie something up is to secure it
in means at home

explanation.surface: Wrapping parcels at home: an easy line of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parcels' looks like the noun but is the verb wrapping SECURES round IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinecures are paid positions requiring little or no work, so jobs of that kind are easy.

clue.text: Queen has hat back to front in northeast India

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: NE is the compass abbreviation for northeast
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the front part of the word is taken to the back, swapping its halves

parts.note: titfer is Cockney rhyming slang for a hat, from tit-for-tat

explanation.surface: A queen visiting northeast India wears her hat the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: TITFER is Cockney rhyming slang (tit-for-tat, hat). 'back to front' moves TIT to the end, making FERTIT, which sits between NE and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefertiti was an ancient Egyptian royal consort, wife of the pharaoh Akhenaten.

clue.text: Wine breaches firm principles

definitions.note: plural, but a single creed sets out a body of principles

indicators.note: breaking through, the wine sits inside the firm's letters

parts.note: Co, short for company, is a firm
red is wine

explanation.surface: A company's principles are compromised by wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaches' puts RED inside CO.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of beliefs, a set of guiding tenets someone lives by.

clue.text: What detects a beer rashly drunk about end of night?

indicators.note: around: the scrambled letters go round the single letter
drunk suggests the letters are tipsily jumbled
the final letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Something that catches a person who downed a beer recklessly late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' scrambles A BEER RASHLY, and 'about' puts that round T.
explanation.definitionFit: A breathalyser is a roadside device that measures alcohol on a motorist's breath.

clue.text: Second husband (Irish) imports a goat product

indicators.note: brings in from outside: the letters before it take the single letter into their middle

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A second husband, an Irishman, imports goods made from goats.
explanation.walkthrough: MO (a moment) is British informal for a second. 'imports' puts A inside MOHIR, between H and IR.
explanation.definitionFit: Mohair is yarn or fabric from the hair of the Angora goat.

clue.text: Battle developing later in court

indicators.note: the word in here means placed within, so the letters before it go inside the ones after

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: developing means changing form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A battle that develops later in a court of law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' rearranges LATER to ATERL, and 'in' puts that inside WOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterloo was the 1815 battle in which Napoleon was finally defeated.

clue.text: Son takes stimulant meal

parts.note: an upper is slang for a stimulant drug

explanation.surface: A son takes a pick-me-up with his evening food.
explanation.definitionFit: Supper is an evening repast, one of the day's meals.

clue.text: Old Roman god seizes unknown ship for mythical hero

indicators.note: grabs and holds, so the other letters sit inside

parts.note: deus is Latin, the Romans' language, for god
Y is an algebraic unknown
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: An ancient Roman deity grabs a vessel for some legendary figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seizes' puts Y and SS inside DEUS, after O.
explanation.definitionFit: Odysseus is the Greek hero of Homer's Odyssey, king of Ithaca.

clue.text: Division short of time? Sign on staff

indicators.note: lacking: the letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a cleft is a split or division

explanation.surface: A department running out of time, and a notice on the staff board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of' drops T from CLEFT. 'staff' is the musical stave, not employees.
explanation.definitionFit: A clef is the symbol at the start of a musical stave fixing the pitch of the notes.

clue.text: Prince initially leaves to promote European winter sport

indicators.note: goes away, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: to plug a product is to promote it

indicators.note: initially means the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A prince leaves to champion a European winter sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' drops P (first letter of 'Prince') from PLUG, giving LUG, then E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: The luge is a small sled raced feet-first down an ice track, a Winter Olympic event.

clue.text: Insectivore, small, reluctant to stand

parts.note: loth means unwilling or reluctant
to bear something is to stand or tolerate it

explanation.surface: A small creature that eats insects is too lazy to stand up.
explanation.walkthrough: Note LOTH, the variant spelling of loath.
explanation.definitionFit: The sloth bear of India feeds largely on termites and ants, so it is an insect-eater.

clue.text: Various TV families in Florida or Cannes event, say

indicators.note: the word in here means placed within, so the letters before it go inside the ones after

parts.note: FL is the postal abbreviation for Florida

indicators.note: various suggests the letters are taken in a different order

explanation.surface: Assorted television families appear in Florida or at a Cannes gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' rearranges TV FAMILIES, and 'in' puts that inside FL.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannes hosts the world's best-known annual movie festival, so it is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Colour variable in a Yorkshire flower

indicators.note: the variable is in the phrase, sitting within the letters of a and the river

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Ure is a river in Yorkshire
Z is an algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire bloom of changeable colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' means a river, not a bloom; the Ure flows through North Yorkshire. 'in' puts Z between A and URE.
explanation.definitionFit: Azure is a bright sky-blue, a shade or hue.

clue.text: Stops working to carry English organ over?

definitions.note: singular, but an over in cricket is made of six balls bowled

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it inside

parts.note: an engine that dies stops working
the liver is an organ

explanation.surface: A machine breaks down while carrying an English organ across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to carry' puts E and LIVER inside DIES. In cricket, an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket over consists of six balls bowled in sequence, so the definition is the group they make.

clue.text: Hollow, or half of it

definitions.meaning: a hollow is a dip or sunken place in a surface
half of 'hollow' is low, and a low is a weather system of low pressure

explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to 'Hollow': its second half is LOW, which in weather forecasts is an area of low atmospheric pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: A hollow is a sunken place in the ground; a low is the meteorological term for the same thing in the atmosphere.

clue.text: Papers I study with bird caught in US garden

parts.note: a den is a private room for work, a study
a tit is a small bird

indicators.note: the word in here means placed within, so the letters before it go inside the ones after

parts.note: Americans call a garden a yard
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone studies papers about a bird trapped in an American garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts C inside YARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Papers is the everyday term for personal documents; an identity card is one such document.

clue.text: After ruckus, fails to find prankster's weapons

indicators.note: the second part comes after the first

parts.note: to make a stink is to cause a fuss or ruckus
a show that bombs is a flop, it fails

explanation.surface: After a row, someone fails to find the joker's weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Stink bombs are small capsules releasing a foul smell, a classic practical joker's device.

clue.text: Café has some meat — missing starter, sweet's filling

indicators.note: the shortened sweet goes inside the meat like a filling

parts.note: a chop is a cut of meat

indicators.note: the first letter is removed

parts.note: toffee's, the possessive of a sweet, is spelt as toffees without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A café's meat dish, starter missing, has a sweet filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing starter' takes T off TOFFEES, giving OFFEES, and 'filling' puts it inside CHOP. 'starter' looks like a first course but means a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffee shop is an informal place selling drinks and light meals, the same as a café.

clue.text: Business clerks ordered to save energy, not layers

parts.note: Co, company, is a business

indicators.note: saving keeps something safely held inside
ordered means put in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Office clerks are told to save energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges CLERKS, and 'to save' holds E inside it, giving CKERELS after CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Male chickens are cockerels; only the hens lay eggs, so these are birds that do not lay.

clue.text: Bunk is high, close to cornice

parts.note: a trip is a drug-induced high

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A bunk bed is set high, near the ceiling moulding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunk' is the slang for nonsense, not a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe and bunk are both informal synonyms for nonsense or rubbish.

clue.text: Not all feel good about old song

indicators.note: turned about, the run of letters is read backwards
only part of the words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Not everyone feels good about an old song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not all' takes EELG from inside 'feel good', and 'about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A glee is an unaccompanied part-song for three or more voices, popular in 18th-century England.

clue.text: Carries out deer or rabbits

definitions.meaning: performs, as in carrying out a task
females of these animals, which share the same name

explanation.definitionFit: To do a task is to carry it out; the females of deer and rabbits are both called by the same word.
